object.value: Name explained as an isomorphic mapping between biology and information science

time.note: Dated by the article as served.

evidence.passage: Paraphrase: the article says that biology can be thought of as an information processing system.

evidence.locator: section "An AI-first approach to drug discovery and biology", next sentence
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: the article says there may be a common underlying structure, an isomorphic mapping, between biology and information science, and that this is the reason for the company’s name.

claims.subject: deepmind
claims.statement: DeepMind published the blog post "AlphaFold: Using AI for scientific discovery" on its CASP13 entry in 2018.

time.note: Year inferred from the text; the served page shows January 15, 2022 (see inferenceRationale).

claims.qualification: The year is inferred, not stated on the page as served, and the served text may differ from the 2018 expression. The CASP13 results are recorded by the models pass from CASP's own sources.

evidence.locator: citation note at end of post
evidence.passage: In Thirteenth Critical Assessment of Techniques for Protein Structure Prediction (Abstracts) 1-4 December 2018.
DeepMind's work on this problem resulted in AlphaFold, which we submitted to CASP this year.

claims.inferenceRationale: The served page carries the date January 15, 2022 (datePublished 2022-01-15), which postdates the events it reports. Its text says AlphaFold was submitted to CASP "this year" and asks readers to cite the CASP13 abstracts of 1-4 December 2018, so the post dates from 2018. The Internet Archive availability API lists a capture at deepmind.com/blog/alphafold/ of 2018-12-03 (not opened). The date is kept at year precision.

claims.subject: aib-doc-dm-alphafold-blog-2018

object.value: AlphaFold presented as a milestone for AI research driving scientific discovery

claims.statement: DeepMind's 2018 AlphaFold post presents the work as "DeepMind's first significant milestone in demonstrating how artificial intelligence research can drive and accelerate new scientific discoveries".
claims.qualification: DeepMind's self-description of its programme, in its words; not an independent assessment.

evidence.passage: We're excited to share DeepMind's first significant milestone in demonstrating how artificial intelligence research can drive and accelerate new scientific discoveries.

claims.subject: aib-doc-dm-alphafold-blog-2018

object.value: DeepMind's statement of its CASP13 ranking (entry A7D)

claims.statement: DeepMind's 2018 post states that its CASP13 entry (A7D) was "placing first in rankings among the teams that entered" and quotes the CASP organisers as calling the progress "unprecedented".
claims.qualification: The developer's own account of an assessment run by others; CASP's own results and the organisers' overview papers are recorded by the models pass and govern. The quoted organisers' phrase is relayed by DeepMind, not taken from a CASP text.

evidence.passage: We're proud to be part of what the CASP organisers have called "unprecedented progress in the ability of computational methods to predict protein structure," placing first in rankings among the teams that entered (our entry is A7D).
